title: Ada and the Asset
premise: Yara Ashgrove, a disgraced intelligence analyst fired from three agencies for asking the wrong questions, discovers that Flight 4471 — mid-air with 212 souls aboard — has been erased from every database on earth. The trail leads to Meridian, a black-site program that trains 'assets' so thoroughly they don't know they've been trained, and Yara realizes he himself was its first successful graduate: his entire career was a scripted loyalty test. Hunted by his former handlers and shadowed by Ada, a defected asset who remembers everything, he must expose and burn the network before it completes an operation that will erase thousands of records — and thousands of people. In the end, Yara chooses truth over the only family he's ever known, broadcasting Meridian's archive at the cost of his own identity, while Ada walks away carrying both their names.
about_author: Jude Lockridge is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent six years writing risk assessments for companies he now refuses to name. He lives off-grid in coastal Maine, where he writes thrillers about systems that eat people.

chapters.title: The Quiet File
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Working dead-end contract analysis in Lisbon, Yara notices a flight number that appears in a cargo manifest but nowhere else — not radar archives, not passenger lists, nothing. His curiosity, the trait that got him fired three times, flickers awake. Emotional beat: restless unease, the itch of a pattern no one else can see.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Twelve Souls
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He confirms Flight 4471 took off from Palma with 212 aboard and simply ceased to exist mid-route. Airlines deny it; regulators have no record. When he calls an old agency contact, the line goes dead mid-sentence. Emotional beat: dread hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Introduced watching Yara from a café across from his flat, running her own counter-investigation into Meridian. She notes his surveillance detail is sloppy — because someone inside Meridian wants him looking. Emotional beat: cold discipline masking grief over what she lost to the program.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. His apartment is tossed with surgical precision; nothing stolen, everything photographed. A burner phone left behind rings once. He flees using tradecraft he never consciously learned — and realizes mid-escape that his body knows things his résumé shouldn't. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-doubt.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ada intercepts Yara at a train station, disarms him in four seconds, and offers a truce: she knows what erased the flight, and she knows what he is. He doesn't believe her until she recites his childhood address — one that exists in no file he's ever found. Emotional beat: hostile alliance forged in mutual fear.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In a safehouse she lays out the program: assets conditioned through manufactured life histories, loyalty tests disguised as careers. Yara's three firings were curriculum. The vanished flight carried a defecting trainer and evidence. Emotional beat: Yara's identity cracking open like ice.

chapters.title: The Handler's Smile
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. His old mentor, Director Caspian Voss, surfaces in person — warm, paternal, offering reinstatement if Yara hands over Ada. Yara realizes Voss was present at every turning point of his life. He plays along, hating how natural obedience feels. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging versus the nausea of manipulation.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Following the flight's last transmission, they reach a decommissioned listening post in the Azores. They find the trainer's dead drop — half a drive of Meridian's operational archive, the other half missing. Ambushers close in; Ada covers Yara's escape, taking a bullet. Emotional beat: first taste of real sacrifice on his behalf.

chapters.title: Field Medicine and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Holed up in a fishing village, Yara patches Ada's wound and, for the first time, tells someone the whole truth of his broken career. She listens without judgment — something no handler ever did. Emotional beat: fragile intimacy; found family taking root in a safehouse.

chapters.title: The Second Half
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Decoding the partial archive reveals Operation WHITEOUT: a coordinated purge that will erase not just records but the people tied to them — witnesses, defectors, loose ends. Execution date: eleven days. The missing archive half sits inside Meridian's Geneva vault. Emotional beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Assets Everywhere
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Testing Ada's theory, Yara maps his old colleagues against Meridian recruitment windows — nearly all of them are unknowing assets, including the friend who once warned him away from the flight. Paranoia becomes strategy: he can turn the network's own training against it. Emotional beat: loneliness transmuted into leverage.

chapters.title: The Friend
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara confronts Marcus, his oldest friend and fellow analyst, who breaks down — he'd been activated weeks ago, ordered to report Yara's movements. Instead of turning him in, Yara recruits him as a double agent. Emotional beat: betrayal met with grace; loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: Geneva, After Dark
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Infiltration of the Meridian vault via a diplomatic gala. Ada works the social engineering; Yara cracks the archive layer using credentials buried in his own conditioning — proof he was built for this exact job. They get the second half of the drive. Alarms trip anyway. Emotional beat: triumph laced with the horror of competence.

chapters.title: What the Archive Says About Me
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Alone with the full archive, Yara reads his own file: recruitment at age nine, every failure engineered, every relationship assigned. Including, ambiguously, instructions regarding Ada. He can't tell if loving her was also scripted. Emotional beat: the book's darkest hour — identity fully dissolved.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Yara shows her the file. Her own entry names him as her designated attachment — designed to keep her controllable. She admits she found hers years ago and stayed anyway, choosing him daily since. Emotional beat: love surviving the revelation that it may have been manufactured.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Captured briefly by Voss, Yara is offered the ultimate rewrite: full memory integration, a new identity, WHITEOUT quietly cancelled for him alone — family, finally, if he surrenders the archive. Voss genuinely believes he's offering mercy. Yara escapes with Marcus's help. Emotional beat: temptation answered with refusal.

chapters.title: Burning the Network
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Three days to WHITEOUT. The plan: seed Meridian's own purge protocol with the archive, making the network erase itself — every asset record, every handler, every hidden account — broadcast publicly. Marcus feeds false confirmations; Ada preps the broadcast node. Emotional beat: grim momentum, everyone spending themselves.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. WHITEOUT begins early. Servers cascade, records die worldwide, and innocent people connected to Meridian start vanishing from existence — including, Yara realizes, the 212 passengers of Flight 4471, still alive somewhere. He must finish the counter-broadcast mid-purge or they stay ghosts forever. Emotional beat: terror at machine-scale consequences.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. At the uplink facility, Ada holds off Voss's extraction team while Yara forces the archive public. Voss offers Yara one last paternal out; Yara answers by pressing transmit. Meridian's files flood every newsroom on earth. Voss, erased by his own system mid-threat, becomes the network's final casualty. Emotional beat: cathartic detonation.

chapters.title: Afterimages
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The fallout: hearings, denials, 212 passengers stepping off a plane in Reykjavik into daylight and cameras. But purged records mean Yara Ashgrove officially never existed — no passport, no history, no legal self. The world believes; the paperwork doesn't care. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by erasure.

chapters.title: Names We Keep
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Ada offers him a choice: she has two clean identities left — enough for one each, or one shared. Yara, who spent ten years being written by others, writes his own line for the first time. They choose new names together, keeping the old ones privately, between them. Emotional beat: quiet rebirth; found family sealed.

chapters.title: Ada and the Asset
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. A year later, under new names in a coastal town, they live unremarkably — until a letter arrives containing a single flight number and no return address. Someone else survived the purge. Ada smiles; Yara already has the map out. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept, story open at the seam.
